toc.title: Tidy history before you share it
Move a branch, pull with rebase, and the golden rule

html:
1What a rebase does

A rebase replays your commits on a new base. On your feature branch you run git rebase main. Git sets your commits aside, moves the branch to the tip of main, and applies the commits again, one by one.

Try it. Rebase feature/search onto main. Your hashes will differ.

git switch feature/search
git rebase main
git log --oneline --decorate --graph

Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/feature/search.
* ad2e9d4 (HEAD -> feature/search) Add results page
* 97b9dd0 Add search box
* 6a20c48 (main) Add footer
* adf13c1 Add header

Each replayed commit has a new parent, so it is a new commit with a new hash. The change it makes is the same.

Part of the commit After the rebase
Changes (the patch) The same
Message, author, author date The same
Parent New: the tip of main
Hash New, for every replayed commit
main Not moved
Old commits Still in the repository (reflog)

The history is now one straight line. Merging the branch into main afterward is a fast-forward.

Tip

. Stand on your own branch and rebase it onto the target. git rebase main moves the branch you are on and never changes main.

2Conflicts during a rebase

A rebase applies commits one at a time, so it can stop at any commit with a conflict. Git names the commit it could not apply. You fix the file, then choose how to go on.

Command What it does
git add <file> then git rebase --continue Keep your resolved version and replay the next commit
git rebase --skip Drop the commit that conflicts and go on
git rebase --abort Stop and put the branch back exactly as it was before

Try it. Resolve one conflict and continue.

git rebase main
git status
git add prices.txt
git rebase --continue

CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in prices.txt
error: could not apply d9f8366... Discount the price
interactive rebase in progress; onto 73c9d35
  (fix conflicts and then run "git rebase --continue")
Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/topic.

Between git status and git add, you edit prices.txt and remove the markers. Status says "interactive rebase in progress" even for a plain rebase.

During a rebase the upper half of the markers (HEAD) is the branch you rebase onto, and the lower half is your commit being replayed. That is the reverse of what many people expect. The same swap applies to git checkout --ours and --theirs: during a rebase, --ours is the branch you rebase onto and --theirs is your own commit (in a merge it is the other way round, module 4).

If several commits change the same lines, the rebase stops once for each. In the lab, three such commits stopped it three times, and after squashing them it stopped once.

Tip

. When a rebase gets confusing, run git rebase --abort. It restores the branch exactly.

3Tidy history before you share it

Amend. git commit --amend replaces the last commit: stage a forgotten file first, then amend. --no-edit keeps the message and -m sets a new one. The result is a new hash.

Interactive rebase. git rebase -i main opens a todo list with one line per commit, oldest first (the reverse of git log). You change the first word of a line or move lines, then save and close.

Word or action What it does
pick Keep the commit as it is
reword Keep the changes, edit the message
squash Meld into the commit above and keep both messages for you to edit
fixup Meld into the commit above and discard this message
drop Delete the commit and its changes
Move a line Reorder the commits

A change to one commit gives every later commit a new hash. The lab edits the list with a script set in GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR.

Try it. Squash a typo fix and drop a debug commit. Your edited list is shown first.

git rebase -i main
git log --oneline main..

pick 12f8210 # Add search box
squash de5fa33 # Fix typo in search box
pick 9eec3d6 # Add results page
pick 6f8d017 # Add filters
drop 8131547 # Debug print

794271a Add filters
aae2271 Add results page
46cccc2 Add search box

Fixup and autosquash. Record a fix as a commit that names its target: git commit --fixup <hash> creates a commit titled fixup! <subject>. Then git rebase -i --autosquash main moves it under the target and marks it fixup for you. The setting rebase.autoSquash true makes this the default for -i.

Try it. GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=true accepts the prepared list without opening an editor.

git commit --fixup ed03d44
GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=true git rebase -i --autosquash main
git log --oneline main..

[feature eb47e53] fixup! Add results page
Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/feature.
a3ce516 Add filters
42d62a9 Add results page
25db6f9 Add search box
Tip

. Fix an older commit with git commit --fixup, then autosquash. It is faster and safer than moving lines in the todo list by hand.

4Move a branch, pull with rebase, and the golden rule

--onto replays only part of a branch somewhere else: git rebase --onto <new base> <old base> <branch>.

Example: topic was started from feature, and feature was then squash-merged into main. A plain git rebase main on topic replays the old feature commits too, and in the lab it stopped on a conflict. git rebase --onto main feature topic replays only the commits after feature, which are the commits of topic. The branch feature is left untouched.

git pull --rebase fetches the new commits from the remote and replays your unpushed commits on top of them. The history stays linear, with no merge commit. Module 7 covers pull in full.

The golden rule: never rebase commits that others already have. A rebase replaces commits, and a teammate's copy of an old commit does not match its new copy. In the lab, Ada rebased a branch she had pushed:

  • A plain git push was rejected as a non-fast-forward.
  • git push --force-with-lease published the rewritten branch.
  • Bob's fetch reported a forced update. His merge pull kept both versions, so the commit appeared twice.
  • Cy, with no work of his own, ran git reset --hard origin/feature/search and matched the remote.
Question Merge Rebase
History shape Keeps real branching and adds a merge commit One straight line, no merge commit
Existing commits Untouched Replaced by new commits with new hashes
Conflicts Resolved once May stop at every replayed commit
Safe on a shared branch Yes No
Undo Revert the merge (module 6) ORIG_HEAD or the reflog
Best for Joining finished work into a shared branch Tidying a private branch, catching up with main
Tip

. Rebase your private branch freely; once others have it, merge instead. If you must rewrite a pushed branch, use --force-with-lease and tell your team.

5Recovering from a bad rebase

A rebase does not delete the old commits at once. Two ways back:

  • ORIG_HEAD holds the branch tip from before the rebase. Run git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD right after the rebase. A later reset or rebase overwrites it.
  • The reflog keeps a history of where each branch pointed. feature/search@{1} is the position before the last change.

Try it. Undo the rebase from section 1.

git reflog show feature/search
git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD

ad2e9d4 feature/search@{0}: rebase (finish): refs/heads/feature/search onto 6a20c48e7e799df5240acffce5ffbd382ad03be5
2ff098c feature/search@{1}: commit: Add results page
HEAD is now at 2ff098c Add results page
Tip

. Make a rescue branch before a risky rebase: git branch rescue. It costs nothing and keeps the old history easy to find.

6Practice Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1After git rebase main, the log shows the same two messages as before, but all the hashes changed. What explains this?

  • AGit rewrote each message while it replayed the commits
  • BEach commit was replayed on a new parent, so it is a new commit
  • CGit merged main into the branch and renamed the commits
  • DGit deleted the old commits and copied them from the reflog
Show the answer

Answer: B. A commit's hash includes its parent, so replaying on a new base creates new commits with the same changes.

S2A rebase stops with "could not apply d9f8366... Discount the price". You have fixed prices.txt and removed the markers. What do you run next?

  • Agit commit, then run git rebase main again
  • Bgit rebase --skip, to keep the file as you fixed it
  • Cgit add prices.txt, then git rebase --continue
  • Dgit merge --abort, to finish replaying the commits
Show the answer

Answer: C. You stage the resolved file and continue, while --skip would drop that commit and your fix with it.

S3Ada rebased feature/search, which she and Bob had both pushed and pulled. Her git push is rejected as a non-fast-forward. What is the safest next step?

  • ARun git push --force so the remote copy matches hers
  • BRun git pull to merge Bob's copy into her branch
  • CDelete the remote branch and push the branch again
  • DRun git push --force-with-lease, then tell Bob to reset
Show the answer

Answer: D. The lease refuses if someone else pushed in the meantime, and Bob must reset because his copy holds the old commits.

S4A branch has the commits "Add cart", "Fix typo" and "WIP". You want the last two folded into "Add cart", with their messages discarded. Which word goes before them in the todo list?

  • Afixup, which melds it in and discards its message
  • Bsquash, which melds it in and keeps its message
  • Creword, which keeps the commit and edits its message
  • Ddrop, which deletes the commit and its changes
Show the answer

Answer: A. fixup melds a commit into the one above and throws its message away, while squash keeps the message.

S5git reflog show feature lists feature@{0}: rebase (finish) above feature@{1}: commit: Add results page. The rebase was a mistake. How do you get the old branch back?

  • ARevert the commit at feature@{0}
  • BCherry-pick the commit at feature@{1}
  • CReset the branch hard to feature@{1}
  • DAbort the finished rebase with --abort
Show the answer

Answer: C. The entry before rebase (finish) is the old tip, and a hard reset moves the branch back to it.

S6topic was started from feature, and feature was squash-merged into main. A plain git rebase main on topic conflicts. Which command replays only the commits of topic?

  • Agit rebase --onto feature main topic
  • Bgit rebase --onto main feature topic
  • Cgit rebase --interactive main topic
  • Dgit rebase --autosquash main topic
Show the answer

Answer: B. --onto <new base> <old base> <branch> replays the commits after feature on top of main.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does git rebase main do to the commits of your branch?

Show the answer

It replays them on top of main as new commits with new hashes.

R2Which three options control a rebase that stopped on a conflict?

Show the answer

--continue, --skip and --abort.

R3Which command creates a commit that autosquash folds into an earlier one?

Show the answer

git commit --fixup <hash>.

R4Which command replaces the last commit instead of adding a new one?

Show the answer

git commit --amend.

R5What does git pull --rebase do with your unpushed commits?

Show the answer

It replays them on top of the fetched commits, with no merge commit.

R6What is the golden rule of rebasing?

Show the answer

Never rebase commits that others already have.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Rebase git rebase main replays your commits on the tip of main; new hashes; straight history
Conflict stops per commit; fix, git add, --continue; or --skip; or --abort
Markers during a rebase the upper half (HEAD) is the branch you rebase onto
Todo list pick, reword, squash, fixup, drop; oldest commit first; move lines to reorder
Amend git commit --amend replaces the last commit; --no-edit keeps the message
Autosquash git commit --fixup <hash>, then git rebase -i --autosquash main
Onto git rebase --onto <new base> <old base> <branch> replays only the commits after the old base
Pull git pull --rebase replays your local commits on the fetched ones
Recovery git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD right away, or branch@{N} from the reflog
